[Resource from qmd at qmd://supabase/apps/docs/content/troubleshooting/vercel-integration-environment-variables-not-syncing-for-persistent-git-branches-b9191e.mdx] 1: ---
2: title = "Vercel Integration: Environment variables explained"
3: topics = [ "platform" ]
4: keywords = []
5: ---
6: 
7: Vercel has three environments, which map to different stages of the deployment lifecycle:
8: 
9: - **Production** is used for the branch configured as the production branch (usually main). Deployments from that branch go to the live site.
10: - **Preview** is used for all other Git branches, including pull requests, feature branches, and persistent branches like staging. If you deploy a staging branch, it still runs under the Preview environment unless you explicitly create a separate environment in Vercel and map that branch to it.
11: - **Development** is only used for local development via the Vercel CLI (`vercel dev`). It allows your local environment to pull env vars from Vercel, but it does not apply to Git branches or deployments on the platform.
12: 
13: ## Creating a staging environment
14: 
15: On the Hobby plan, staging is implemented by scoping Preview environment variables to a branch. On the Pro plan, staging can be configured as a dedicated environment with its own settings.
16: 
17: You can create a dedicated environment (Vercel Pro):
18: 
19: 1. Go to `Project` → `Settings` → `Environments`
20: 2. Click `Create Environment`
21: 3. Name it `staging`
22: 4. Enable `Branch Tracking` and select the `staging` branch
23: 5. Add environment variables scoped to this environment
24: 
25: With this setup, the staging branch deploys to its own environment and is fully separate from Preview and Production.
26:

[Resource from qmd at qmd://supabase/apps/docs/content/guides/deployment/branching/integrations.mdx] 1: ---
2: title: 'Integrations'
3: description: 'Use Supabase branching with hosting providers and other tools.'
4: subtitle: 'Use Supabase branching with hosting providers and other tools'
5: ---
6: 
7: Branching works with hosting providers that support preview deployments. Learn how to integrate Supabase branching with various platforms and tools.
8: 
9: ## Hosting providers
10: 
11: With the Supabase branching integration, you can sync the Git branch used by the hosting provider with the corresponding Supabase preview branch. This means that the preview deployment built by your hosting provider is matched to the correct database schema, edge functions, and other Supabase configurations.
12: 
13: ### Vercel
14: 
15: Install the Vercel integration:
16: 
17: - From the [Vercel marketplace](https://vercel.com/integrations/supabase) or
18: - By clicking the blue `Deploy` button in a Supabase example app's `README` file
19: 
20: <Admonition type="note" title="Vercel GitHub integration also required.">
21: 
22: For branching to work with Vercel, you also need the [Vercel GitHub integration](https://vercel.com/docs/deployments/git/vercel-for-github).
23: 
24: </Admonition>
25: 
26: And make sure you have [connected](/dashboard/org/_/integrations) your Supabase project to your Vercel project.
27: 
28: Supabase automatically updates your Vercel project with the correct environment variables for the corresponding preview branches. The synchronization happens at the time of Pull Request being opened, not at the time of branch creation.
29: 
30: As branching integration is tied to the Preview Deployments feature in Vercel, there are possible race conditions between Supabase setting correct variables, and Vercel running a deployment process. Because of that, Supabase is always automatically re-deploying the most recent deployment of the given pull request.

Because of that, Supabase is always automatically re-deploying the most recent deployment of the given pull request.
31:

Per `supabase/apps/docs/content/guides/deployment/branching/integrations.mdx` (Vercel section): Supabase *does* auto-sync Vercel preview env vars to match the branch's preview database — but this requires the **Vercel GitHub integration** installed in addition to the Supabase↔Vercel connection, and sync happens **when the PR is opened**, not when the branch is created. If you create the branch after the PR already exists (or are missing the GitHub integration), preview builds keep the production connection string.

Check: (1) Vercel GitHub integration is installed, (2) Supabase project is connected under Vercel dashboard's Integrations, (3) re-trigger/re-open the PR so sync fires. If all set and it still fails, that doc notes race conditions are handled by Supabase auto-redeploying the latest deployment for the PR — worth confirming a redeploy actually occurred.
